summary_rationale: Capital One has evolved from a 1994 monoline credit card spin-off into a $672.9 billion-asset, AWS cloud-native national bank with ~85% FDIC-insured deposit funding ($480.7 billion total deposits in Q3 2026) and a newly vertically integrated closed-loop payment network via the May 2025 Discover Financial Services acquisition ($51.8 billion) and the April 2026 Brex corporate spend acquisition ($5.15 billion). Completing the consumer debit migration onto PULSE by mid-2026 unlocks Durbin-exempt network economics toward management's $2.7 billion pre-tax run-rate synergy target by 2027, lifting Q3 2026 net interest margin to 8.41% and consolidated net charge-off rate down to 2.73% (3.98% in Domestic Card) with a 13.8% CET1 ratio and 4.92% allowance coverage. Nevertheless, Capital One remains structurally a credit-cyclical lender with material non-prime and near-prime card and auto exposure, elevated integration and compliance remediation demands from Discover's legacy consent orders, and ongoing regulatory scrutiny of card fees—warranting a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality classification with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health (watching the sequential uptick in 30+ day delinquencies to 3.41% in Q3 2026 and post-merger integration execution).
